reader.requirement: A CALL naming a program-name shared by several programs of the run unit must resolve by the 1985 program-name scope rules: a program directly contained in the caller first, then a COMMON program directly contained in a program that contains the caller (unless the caller is that common program or within it), otherwise the separately compiled program, for literal and identifier targets alike.

edition-consulted.switches: arm 2 and the recursive exception read the RECURSIVE attribute, which no COBOL-85 program has; not an edition test
ExternalizedNameInEdition: an identifier's value formed in the edition's name spelling

reader.edition-search: grep of ProgramNameScope.cs, ProgramTable.cs, CallBinder.cs and CallEmitter.cs for Edition|Dialect|ConstructRegistry: the resolution arms consult no edition
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no (2023's recursive-common exception cannot arise at 85)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f02_04 covers one nested-versus-separate case; the common arm, the caller-inside-common exception, a sibling's view of a non-common nested program and identifier targets were probed here

probes.printed: M1/M2 NESTED SUB IN MAINP (literal and identifier); M3 from KID: SEPARATE SUB twice (a non-common sibling is not visible); A calls CSB: COMMON CSB IN OUTER; C inside CSB calls CSB: SEPARATE CSB twice; B in A by identifier: COMMON CSB IN OUTER
probes.expected: GR4 mechanism a, b and c

probes.printed: the common CSB calling CSB: SEPARATE CSB; GGK (indirectly contained) calls CSB: COMMON CSB
probes.expected: the caller is the common program: the separately compiled one is called; an indirect container reaches the common program

citations.check: OK  §1985:X.5.2.4 GR4  the text is in the clause or rule: "that common program is called unless the calling program is contained within that common program"
OK  §1985:X.1.3.8.1  the text is in the clause or rule: "except programs it directly or indirectly contains"

reader.notes: One shared scope walk (ProgramNameScope) answers the run-time resolver and the binder; arms 1 and 3 match the 1985 scope rules 1 and 2, with the separately compiled program as the fallback. Classes a, d and f do not apply to name resolution.

refuter.evidence: Probe probes-refute-c07/src/rc1.cob at --std 85 (runs/rc1-002, EXIT 0): a non-common grandchild GSUB (in KA) is not visible to RC1, which calls the separately compiled GSUB by literal and identifier (SEPARATE GSUB twice); KA calling CX, a common program directly contained in sibling KB (which does not contain KA), gets the separately compiled CX (SEPARATE CX); KB calling its own common child gets COMMON CX IN KB. rc1-001 (CALL KB from KA, a non-common sibling with no separate KB) ended EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND, which is right: KB is not referable from KA. The run-time message cites §2023:14.9.4.4 GR3b at --std 85 (diagnostic text only, outside this rule). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:X.5.2.4 GR4 ... resolved by using the scope of names conventions for program-names'.
